words.en: Lacking firmness, resilience, or muscle tone; soft and limp.

words.tr:
n. 旗；旗帜；信号旗；
v. 用旗标记；
words.ex: The flag waves in the wind.
words.ex_cn: 旗帜在风中飘扬。
words.en: A flag is a piece of cloth with a special design or colors that is used as a symbol, or to give a signal.

words.tr: adj. 明目张胆的；丑恶可耻的；公然的
words.ex: He made a flagrant mistake during the game.
words.ex_cn: 他在比赛中犯了一个明显的错误。
words.en: If you describe an action as flagrant, you mean that it is done in an open and obvious way and is intended to shock or offend people.

words.ex: She has a flair for painting.
words.ex_cn: 她有绘画的天赋。
words.en: If you have a flair for a particular activity, you have a natural ability to do it well.

words.tr: adj. 艳丽的；炫耀的；神气活现的
words.ex: He wears flamboyant clothes to stand out.
words.ex_cn: 他穿著華麗的衣服來引人注目。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is flamboyant, you mean that they are very noticeable, stylish, and exciting.

words.tr:
v. 拍动；摆动；
n. 薄片；
words.ex: The bird flaps its wings to fly.
words.ex_cn: 鸟拍动翅膀飞翔。
words.en: A flap is a piece of cloth, paper, skin etc that is fixed at one edge to a surface, which you can lift up easily. If something such as a piece of cloth or paper flaps or if you flap it, it moves quickly up and down or from side to side.

words.tr:
v. 奉承；讨好
adj. 更平坦的；更扁平的；“flat”的比较级
adv. 更平直地；更直截了当地；“flat”的比较级
words.ex: He flatters his boss to get a raise.
words.ex_cn: 他奉承老板以获得加薪。
words.en: If someone flatters you, they praise you in an exaggerated way that may be sincere or may be intended to persuade you to do something.

words.ex: He likes to flaunt his new car.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢炫耀他的新车。
words.en: If you flaunt something, you show it off in a way that is intended to attract people's attention and make them envious.

words.tr:
n. 刚长齐羽毛学飞的幼鸟
adj. 新形成的；无经验的
v. 羽毛长成；用羽毛盖上；装上羽毛；“fledge”的现在分词
words.ex: The fledgling bird tried to fly for the first time.
words.ex_cn: 这只幼鸟第一次尝试飞翔。
words.en: A fledgling is a young bird that has just grown its feathers and is learning to fly. It can also refer to a person or organization that is new and inexperienced.

words.tr:
v. 轻弹；轻击；轻拂；忽然摇动
n. 轻弹；轻拂；快速的轻打
words.ex: He flicked the light switch on.
words.ex_cn: 他 flick 了一下电灯开关。
words.en: To move or hit something with a quick, sharp movement.

words.tr: adj. 轻浮的；反复无常的
words.ex: She was known for her flighty behavior.
words.ex_cn: 她以轻浮的行为而闻名。
words.en: If you describe someone as flighty, you disapprove of them because they are not very serious or reliable and keep changing from one interest, idea, or partner to another.

words.tr:
adj. 轻而薄的；易坏的；不足信的
n. 复写纸；薄纸副本
words.ex: The flimsy chair broke when he sat on it.
words.ex_cn: 那把脆弱的椅子当他坐上去时就断了。
words.en: Something that is flimsy is not very strong or solid, and therefore easily damaged or destroyed.

words.ex: He didn't flinch when the needle touched his skin.
words.ex_cn: 当针碰到他的皮肤时，他没有退缩。
words.en: If you flinch, you make a small sudden movement, especially when something surprises you or hurts you.

words.tr: adj. 轻率的；轻浮的；不严肃的
words.ex: His flippant remarks annoyed everyone at the meeting.
words.ex_cn: 他轻率的言论让会议上的每个人都感到恼火。
words.en: If you describe a person or what they say as flippant, you are criticizing them because you think they are not taking something as seriously as they should.

words.tr: adj. 红润的；华丽的；过分装饰的
words.ex: Her cheeks were florid after running in the cold.
words.ex_cn: 她在寒冷中跑步后，脸颊变得红润。
words.en: If you describe something as florid, you mean that it is complicated and elaborate rather than plain and simple.

words.tr:
v. 挣扎；深陷困境
n. 比目鱼
words.ex: The fish floundered in the shallow water.
words.ex_cn: 鱼在浅水中挣扎。
words.en: If you flounder, you experience great difficulties and are likely to fail completely.

words.tr:
v. 藐视；轻视；嘲笑
n. 嘲弄；轻视
words.ex: He flouts the rules every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天都无视规则。
words.en: If you flout something such as a law, an order, or an accepted way of behaving, you deliberately do not obey it or follow it.

words.ex: The fluorescent lamp lights up the room quickly.
words.ex_cn: 荧光灯很快照亮了房间。
words.en: Fluorescent substances produce bright light of a particular color when they are exposed to light of a different wavelength.

words.tr:
v. 使惊慌失措；使慌张
n. 慌张；慌乱
words.ex: He got flustered when the teacher asked him a question.
words.ex_cn: 当老师问他问题时，他变得慌乱了。
words.en: If you fluster someone, you make them feel nervous and confused by rushing them or by making it difficult for them to concentrate on what they are doing.

words.ex: He tries to foment trouble between the neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 他试图在邻居之间挑起纠纷。
words.en: If someone foments trouble or violent opposition, they cause it to develop.

words.tr:
n. 箔；陪衬物
v. 阻止；挫败
words.ex: He used foil to wrap the sandwich.
words.ex_cn: 他用锡纸包住了三明治。
words.en: To prevent someone from succeeding in their plans or intentions, especially by doing something clever or unexpected.

words.tr: adj. 莽撞的；有勇无谋的
words.ex: He made a foolhardy decision to climb the mountain alone.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个有勇无谋的决定，独自去爬山。
words.en: If you describe behavior or an action as foolhardy, you mean that it is very risky because it shows a lack of thought or care for the possible consequences.

words.tr:
v. 搜寻；（动物）觅食；
n. 饲料；草料；
words.ex: The bear forages for berries in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这只熊在森林里搜寻浆果。
words.en: If you forage, you search for food or other supplies. Forage can also refer to food for animals, especially when it is grown or collected.

words.ex: He will forego dessert to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 为了保持健康，他将放弃甜点。
words.en: To forego something means to decide not to have or do something that you would like to have or do.

words.ex: The detective used forensic evidence to solve the case.
words.ex_cn: 侦探使用法医证据破了案。
words.en: Relating to or denoting the application of scientific methods and techniques to the investigation of crime.

words.tr: v. 预先阻止；抢先一步
words.ex: He forestalls problems by planning ahead.
words.ex_cn: 他通过提前计划来防止问题。
words.en: To forestall something means to prevent it from happening or to act before someone else does in order to prevent them from doing something.

words.tr:
n. 没收物；罚金
v. 丧失；被没收
words.ex: He had to pay a forfeit for breaking the rule.
words.ex_cn: 他因违反规定不得不支付没收物。
words.en: If you forfeit something, you lose it or are forced to give it up because you have broken a rule or done something wrong.

words.tr:
n. 锻造车间；
v. 建立（联系等）；
words.ex: The blacksmith works in the forge every morning.
words.ex_cn: 铁匠每天早上都在锻造车间工作。
words.en: To forge something means to create it, especially by using considerable effort or skill. It can also mean to make or produce something, especially with some difficulty or effort. Additionally, it refers to the act of making a copy or imitation of something with the intent to deceive.

words.ex: He will forgo dessert to stay healthy.
words.ex_cn: 为了保持健康，他将放弃甜点。
words.en: If you forgo something, you decide to do without it, even though you would like it.

words.tr: adj. 绝望的；孤立无助的；被弃置的
words.ex: The forlorn dog sat by the door, waiting for its owner.
words.ex_cn: 那条孤单的狗坐在门边，等待它的主人。
words.en: If someone is forlorn, they feel alone and unhappy.

words.ex: He will not forsake his family.
words.ex_cn: 他不会抛弃他的家人。
words.en: If you forsake someone, you leave them when you should have stayed, or you stop helping them or looking after them.

words.ex: He showed great fortitude during the hard times.
words.ex_cn: 他在艰难时期展现了极大的毅力。
words.en: Fortitude is the mental and emotional strength that enables a person to face difficulty, danger, or pain without fear.

words.ex: It was fortuitous that he found his keys just before leaving.
words.ex_cn: 他在出发前刚好找到钥匙，真是幸运。
words.en: If you describe something as fortuitous, you mean that it happens by chance rather than by anyone's planning or intention.

words.tr:
adj. 肮脏恶臭的；
v. 对…犯规；
words.ex: The foul smell came from the garbage bin.
words.ex_cn: 那股恶臭来自垃圾桶。
words.en: If you describe something as foul, you mean it is dirty and smells or tastes unpleasant. In sports, a foul is an act that is against the rules of the game.

words.ex: Steve Jobs is the founder of Apple.
words.ex_cn: 史蒂夫·乔布斯是苹果公司的创办者。
words.en: A founder is someone who establishes an organization, company, or institution. As a verb, it means to fail or collapse, especially in terms of a plan or a ship sinking.

words.ex: He fractured his arm during the soccer game.
words.ex_cn: 他在足球比赛中摔断了手臂。
words.en: If something such as a bone fractures or is fractured, it breaks or cracks.

words.ex: He bought a franchise to open a coffee shop.
words.ex_cn: 他购买了一个特许经营权来开一家咖啡店。
words.en: A franchise is an authorization granted by a government or company to an individual or group enabling them to carry out specified commercial activities, e.g., acting as an agent for a company's products.

words.ex: She was frantic to catch the last bus.
words.ex_cn: 她急忙赶着赶最后一班公交车。
words.en: If someone is frantic, they are behaving in a wild and desperate way, often because they are frightened or worried.

words.ex: He joined a fraternity at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学加入了兄弟会。
words.en: Fraternity refers to a group of people sharing a common profession or interests, or a feeling of friendship and mutual support within a group.

words.ex: The children were running in a frenetic way around the room.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们在房间里发狂似的跑来跑去。
words.en: If you describe an activity as frenetic, you mean that it is fast and energetic, but rather uncontrolled and often not very well organized.

words.tr:
n. 狂乱；狂暴；狂怒
v. 使狂乱；使狂怒
words.ex: The crowd went into a frenzy when the singer appeared.
words.ex_cn: 当歌手出现时，人群陷入了狂热。
words.en: A frenzy is a state of uncontrolled excitement or wild behavior.

words.ex: The fretful child cried all night.
words.ex_cn: 这个烦躁的孩子整晚都在哭。
words.en: If someone is fretful, they behave in a way that shows that they are worried or unhappy about something.

words.tr: adj. 寒冷的；冷淡的；性冷淡的（女子）
words.ex: The water is frigid in winter.
words.ex_cn: 冬天的水很冰冷。
words.en: Frigid means extremely cold in temperature or lacking warmth or enthusiasm.

words.ex: The fringe of the forest is full of wildflowers.
words.ex_cn: 森林的边缘长满了野花。
words.en: The outer, marginal, or extreme part of an area, group, or sphere of activity.

words.ex: The frisky puppy was bouncing around the room.
words.ex_cn: 那只活泼的小狗在房间里蹦来蹦去。
words.en: If you describe a person or animal as frisky, you mean they are lively and playful.

words.ex: He ignored the frivolous complaint and focused on the real issue.
words.ex_cn: 他忽略了这个无关紧要的投诉，专注于真正的问题。
words.en: If you describe someone as frivolous, you mean they behave in a silly or light-hearted way, rather than being serious and sensible.

words.ex: He is frugal with his money.
words.ex_cn: 他花钱很节俭。
words.en: If you describe someone as frugal, you mean that they are careful about spending money and use things only when they need to.

words.tr: n. 取得成果；实现；完成
words.ex: The project finally came to fruition after years of hard work.
words.ex_cn: 经过多年的努力，这个项目终于完成了。
words.en: The realization or fulfillment of a plan or project.

words.ex: The fugitive hid in the woods for weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这名逃亡者在树林里躲了几个星期。
words.en: A fugitive is someone who is running away or hiding, usually in order to avoid being caught by the police.

words.tr: adj. 浓烈的；醇厚的；圆润的（音质）
words.ex: The wine had a full-bodied flavor with hints of blackberry and oak.
words.ex_cn: 这款酒口感浓郁，带有黑莓和橡木的香气。
words.en: Having a rich, strong flavor or quality.

words.tr: adj. 狂怒的；暴怒的；激烈的
words.ex: He was furious when he lost his keys.
words.ex_cn: 他丢了钥匙时非常生气。
words.en: If someone is furious, they are extremely angry.

words.ex: The new song caused a furor among teenagers.
words.ex_cn: 这首歌在青少年中引起了狂热。
words.en: A furor is a very angry or excited reaction by people to something.

words.tr: n. 城河；壕坑; n. （Foss）人名；（德、英、法、西、瑞典）福斯
words.ex: The castle is surrounded by a deep foss.
words.ex_cn: 城堡被一条深城河环绕。
words.en: A fossilized remnant or trace of an organism from a past geological age.

words.ex: It was futile to try to fix the broken clock.
words.ex_cn: 试图修理坏掉的钟表是徒劳的。
words.en: If you say that something is futile, you mean there is no point in doing it, usually because it has no chance of succeeding.

words.ex: The children's laughter brought gaiety to the party.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们的笑声为派对带来了欢乐。
words.en: Gaiety is a feeling, attitude, or atmosphere of liveliness and fun.

words.ex: No one can gainsay the truth.
words.ex_cn: 没有人能否认这个事实。
words.en: If there is no gainsaying something, it is not possible to deny that it is true or that it exists.

words.ex: The old man walked with a slow gait.
words.ex_cn: 老人走路步伐缓慢。
words.en: A person's manner of walking.

words.ex: She fought gamely despite her injuries.
words.ex_cn: 尽管受了伤，她还是勇敢地战斗。
words.en: In a brave and spirited manner; with pluck.

words.tr:
v. 目瞪口呆地看；裂开
n. 目瞪口呆地看；裂口
words.ex: The children gape at the magic show.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们张大嘴看着魔术表演。
words.en: To open the mouth wide; to stare with open mouth, as in wonder.

words.tr: v. 混淆；曲解；断章取义
words.ex: He garbled the message so no one understood it.
words.ex_cn: 他把消息说得乱七八糟，没人能听懂。
words.en: If you garble something, you distort or confuse it so that it is difficult to understand.

words.ex: The elephant was gargantuan compared to the dog.
words.ex_cn: 这只大象比起狗来说巨大无比。
words.en: If you say that something is gargantuan, you are emphasizing that it is very large.

words.tr: adj. 俗艳的；花哨的；过分装饰的
words.ex: The room was decorated in a garish pink that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间被装饰成刺眼的粉红色，令人眼睛不适。
words.en: If you describe something as garish, you mean that it is excessively bright, colorful, or elaborate in a way that is considered tasteless or unattractive.

words.ex: He garnered food for the winter.
words.ex_cn: 他贮藏了过冬的食物。
words.en: To gather or collect something, especially information or support.

words.tr:
v. （在食物上）加装饰菜；装饰
n. （食物上的）装饰菜；装饰
words.ex: She puts a lemon slice to garnish the drink.
words.ex_cn: 她放一片柠檬来装饰这杯饮料。
words.en: To garnish something means to decorate it with something, especially food with small amounts of different foods.

words.tr: adj. 絮聒的；饶舌的；多嘴的
words.ex: He is garrulous and talks too much.
words.ex_cn: 他话很多，说个不停。
words.en: If you describe someone as garrulous, you mean that they talk a lot, especially about things that are not important.

words.ex: The room was decorated with gaudy colors that hurt the eyes.
words.ex_cn: 房间用俗丽的颜色装饰，刺眼。
words.en: If you describe something as gaudy, you mean that it is very brightly coloured and showy, but not in an attractive way.

words.tr: n. 测量仪器；规格；评估；
words.ex: The mechanic used a gauge to check the tire pressure.
words.ex_cn: 机械师用一个测量仪器来检查轮胎气压。
words.en: A gauge is a device that measures the amount or quantity of something and shows the measurement in a form that is easy to read, such as a dial or a digital display.

words.tr:
n. 凝视；注视；
v. 凝视；注视；
words.ex: His gaze fixed on the sunset.
words.ex_cn: 他的凝视固定在日落上。
words.en: If you gaze at someone or something, you look steadily at them for a long time, for example because you find them attractive or interesting, or because you are thinking about something else.

words.ex: He shifted the gear to slow down the car.
words.ex_cn: 他换挡以减慢车速。
words.en: Gear refers to a toothed wheel that works with others to alter the relation between the speed of a driving mechanism (such as the engine of a vehicle) and the speed of the driven parts (the wheels). It can also mean equipment that is used for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The genesis of the story is a simple dream.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的起源是一个简单的梦。
words.en: The origin or mode of formation of something.

words.tr: adj. 亲切的；和蔼的；温暖的
words.ex: He is a genial man who always smiles.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个和蔼可亲的人，总是面带微笑。
words.en: Friendly and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 文雅的；有教养的；上流社会的；装绅士派头的
words.ex: She spoke in a genteel way at the dinner party.
words.ex_cn: 她在晚宴上说话很文雅。
words.en: Someone who is genteel behaves in a polite and refined way, often in a manner that is considered typical of someone from a high social class.

words.ex: The gentry owned most of the land in the old village.
words.ex_cn: 绅士阶层拥有这个古老村庄的大部分土地。
words.en: The gentry are people of high social class, especially in the past.

words.ex: The seeds germinate in warm soil.
words.ex_cn: 种子在温暖的土壤中发芽。
words.en: To germinate means to begin to grow or develop, especially for a seed or spore.

words.tr:
adj. 可怕的；恐怖的；惨白的；令人不快的
adv. 可怖地；惨白地
words.ex: The ghost looked ghastly in the dark.
words.ex_cn: 那个幽灵在黑暗中看起来吓人极了。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as ghastly, you mean that they are extremely unpleasant or shocking.

words.tr: adj. 使人晕眩的；头晕的；轻浮的
words.ex: She felt giddy after spinning around.
words.ex_cn: 她转圈后感到头晕目眩。
words.en: If you feel giddy, you feel unsteady and think that you are about to fall over, usually because you are not well or because you are excited or frightened.

words.ex: The elephant is gigantic compared to a dog.
words.ex_cn: 这头大象相比狗来说是巨大的。
words.en: If you describe something as gigantic, you are emphasizing that it is extremely large in size, amount, or degree.

words.ex: The ad used a cheap gimmick to attract customers.
words.ex_cn: 这个广告用了一个廉价的噱头来吸引顾客。
words.en: A gimmick is a trick or device intended to attract attention, publicity, or trade.

words.ex: Can you tell me the gist of the story?
words.ex_cn: 你能告诉我这个故事的要点吗？
words.en: The main or essential part of a matter.

words.ex: The dress gave her a lot of glamour.
words.ex_cn: 这条裙子给她增添了许多魅力。
words.en: If someone or something has glamour, they are attractive and exciting in a way that is not ordinary.

words.ex: The glare of the sun made it hard to see.
words.ex_cn: 阳光的刺眼使我看不清。
words.en: If you glare at someone, you look at them with an angry expression on your face. Glare is also a very bright light that is uncomfortable to look at.

words.tr:
v. 上釉；上玻璃；浇浆汁于；变呆滞
n. 釉料；光滑面；覆罩的一层
words.ex: The potter glazes the clay bowl before firing it.
words.ex_cn: 陶匠在烧制前给陶碗上釉。
words.en: To glaze means to fit panes of glass into a window frame or similar structure. It can also refer to the process of applying a glossy, often transparent, coating to pottery or other materials.

words.ex: The bird glide smoothly over the lake.
words.ex_cn: 鸟儿在湖面上滑行。
words.en: To move smoothly and continuously along, as if without effort or resistance.

words.tr:
v. 闪亮；闪光
n. 闪亮；闪光
words.ex: The sun made the knife glint.
words.ex_cn: 阳光使刀子闪亮。
words.en: If something glints, it produces or reflects a quick flash of light.

words.tr:
v. 闪光；闪耀
n. 闪光；闪耀
words.ex: The dew glistens on the grass in the morning.
words.ex_cn: 早晨露珠在草地上闪闪发亮。
words.en: If something glistens, it shines, usually because it is wet or oily.

words.tr:
n. 闪耀；闪烁；小发光物
v. 闪耀；闪亮；流露（感情）
words.ex: The glitter of the stars lit up the night sky.
words.ex_cn: 星星的闪耀照亮了夜空。
words.en: If something glitters, light comes from or is reflected off different parts of it.

words.tr: v. 幸灾乐祸；沾沾自喜；满足地看
words.ex: He gloats when his rival loses the game.
words.ex_cn: 当他的对手输掉比赛时，他幸灾乐祸。
words.en: To gloat means to observe or think about something with triumphant and often malicious satisfaction, gratification, or delight.

words.ex: The book has a gloss at the bottom of each page.
words.ex_cn: 这本书每页底部都有注释。
words.en: A gloss is a bright shine on the surface of something. It can also refer to a superficial appearance or interpretation that conceals the true nature of something.

words.tr:
n. （赶牲畜的）尖头棒；激励；刺激
v. 刺激；驱使
words.ex: The farmer used a goad to guide the oxen.
words.ex_cn: 农夫用一根尖头棒赶牛。
words.en: If you goad someone, you deliberately make them feel angry or irritated, often causing them to react by doing something.

words.ex: He sings gospel music every Sunday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周日唱福音音乐。
words.en: The teachings of Jesus and the apostles, especially as contained in the first four books of the New Testament, known as the Gospels.

words.ex: The gardener did a graft on the apple tree.
words.ex_cn: 园丁在苹果树上进行了嫁接。
words.en: Graft can refer to the act of joining parts from different plants so that they grow as one plant, or to the act of transferring living tissue from one part of the body to another. It can also refer to the practice of using one's position to gain money or advantages dishonestly.

words.tr: adj. 词藻浮华的；夸大的；做作的
words.ex: He gave a grandiloquent speech full of big words.
words.ex_cn: 他发表了一篇充满华丽辞藻的演讲。
words.en: If you describe someone's language as grandiloquent, you mean that it is extremely formal, elaborate, or exaggerated, and is used to impress people.

words.ex: The palace has a grandiose design with tall columns and golden domes.
words.ex_cn: 这座宫殿有着宏伟的设计，配有高大的柱子和金色的圆顶。
words.en: If you describe something as grandiose, you mean it is larger or more elaborate than necessary, or it is intended to seem very impressive or magnificent.

words.tr:
n. 格栅
adj. 磨擦的；刺耳的
v. 磨碎；磨擦；（使）烦躁；发出磨擦声；“grate”的现在分词
words.ex: The sound of the grating metal door echoed through the hallway.
words.ex_cn: 金属门刺耳的声音在走廊里回荡。
words.en: A grating is a flat frame of metal bars or a similar structure, used to cover a hole or window, or as a partition. It can also refer to a harsh, discordant sound.

words.tr: adj. 无故的；无必要的；无偿的；免费的
words.ex: He made a gratuitous comment about her clothes.
words.ex_cn: 他对她的衣服做了毫无必要的评论。
words.en: If you describe something as gratuitous, you mean that it is unnecessary, and often harmful or upsetting.

words.ex: Dolphins are gregarious animals that swim in groups.
words.ex_cn: 海豚是群居动物，成群游泳。
words.en: Someone who is gregarious enjoys being with other people.

words.tr: adj. 严厉的；严峻的；冷酷无情的；坚定的；可怕的
words.ex: He had a grim look on his face.
words.ex_cn: 他脸上带着严峻的表情。
words.en: If a situation or piece of news is grim, it is very serious, unpleasant, and depressing.

words.tr:
n. 怨恨；积怨；嫌隙
v. 勉强做；不情愿地给；吝惜
words.ex: He holds a grudge against his brother.
words.ex_cn: 他对他哥哥心怀怨恨。
words.en: A grudge is a persistent feeling of ill will or resentment resulting from a past insult or injury.

words.ex: The movie showed a gruesome accident.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影展示了一起令人毛骨悚然的事故。
words.en: Something that is gruesome is extremely unpleasant and shocking, especially because it involves death or injury.

words.tr:
v. 发牢骚；抱怨；轰鸣
n. 怨言；牢骚；轰隆声
words.ex: He grumbles when he has to wake up early.
words.ex_cn: 他不得不早起时就会抱怨。
words.en: If someone grumbles, they complain about something in a bad-tempered way.

words.ex: He used guile to trick the guard.
words.ex_cn: 他用诡计骗过了守卫。
words.en: Guile is the quality of being skilled at deceiving people in order to achieve something.

words.ex: He is gullible and believes every story he hears.
words.ex_cn: 他很容易受骗，相信每一个他听到的故事。
words.en: If you describe someone as gullible, you mean they are easily tricked because they are too trusting.

words.ex: He is a guru in computer programming.
words.ex_cn: 他是计算机编程方面的专家。
words.en: A guru is a person who is very skilled and knowledgeable in a particular subject, and who gives advice and guidance to others.

words.tr:
v. 喷涌；滔滔不绝地说
n. 涌出；喷出
words.ex: Water gushed from the broken pipe.
words.ex_cn: 水从破裂的管道中喷涌而出。
words.en: If someone gushes, they express their admiration or pleasure in an exaggerated way.

words.tr: adj. 缺乏勇气的；怯懦的
words.ex: He was gutless and refused to speak up.
words.ex_cn: 他很懦弱，不敢站出来说话。
words.en: If you describe someone as gutless, you think they have a weak character and lack courage or determination.

words.tr: adj. 陈腐的；陈词滥调的；老生常谈的
words.ex: His jokes are hackneyed and boring.
words.ex_cn: 他的笑话陈腐又无聊。
words.en: If you describe something as hackneyed, you mean that it is unoriginal and has been used so often that it is no longer interesting.

words.tr:
n. 冰雹；
v. 把…誉为；
words.ex: The hail broke many car windows.
words.ex_cn: 冰雹打碎了许多汽车窗户。
words.en: Hail is small balls of ice that fall like rain from the sky. It can also mean to call out to someone in order to attract their attention, or to praise someone enthusiastically.

words.ex: They hallow the old church on Halloween.
words.ex_cn: 他们在万圣节时敬拜那座老教堂。
words.en: To make holy or set apart as holy; to honor as sacred.

words.ex: He arranged the books in a haphazard way.
words.ex_cn: 他随意地摆放了书。
words.en: If you describe something as haphazard, you are critical of it because it is not at all organized or is not arranged according to a plan.

words.tr: adj. 通过经历而变得顽强的；坚毅的；冷酷无情的
words.ex: The hard-bitten soldier never gave up, even in the face of overwhelming odds.
words.ex_cn: 面对压倒性的劣势，这位顽强的士兵也从未放弃。
words.en: If you describe someone as hard-bitten, you mean that they have been through a lot of difficult or unpleasant experiences and are tough as a result.

words.tr: adj. 匆忙的；草率的；急躁的
words.ex: He made a hasty decision and regretted it.
words.ex_cn: 他做了一个仓促的决定，后来后悔了。
words.en: If you describe a person or their behavior as hasty, you mean that they are acting too quickly, without thinking carefully, often with unwanted results.

words.ex: The bird hatched her eggs after three weeks.
words.ex_cn: 这只鸟在三周后孵出了她的蛋。
words.en: To hatch means to cause an egg to break open so that a young animal can come out, or to plan secretly with other people to do something bad or illegal.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；高傲自大的
words.ex: He gave a haughty smile when he won the prize.
words.ex_cn: 他赢得奖品时露出了傲慢的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as haughty, you mean that they behave in a proud, unfriendly way, because they think that they are better than other people.

words.ex: The memory of the accident still haunts him.
words.ex_cn: 那场事故的记忆仍然长期困扰着他。
words.en: If something unpleasant haunts you, you keep thinking or worrying about it over a long period of time. A place that is haunted is believed to be visited regularly by a ghost.

words.tr: n. 大破坏；大毁坏；大混乱；
words.ex: The storm caused havoc in the small town.
words.ex_cn: 风暴给这个小镇带来了大破坏。
words.en: If you describe something as havoc, you mean that it causes a great deal of disorder, confusion, or destruction.

words.ex: The chemicals are hazardous to health.
words.ex_cn: 这些化学物质对健康有危险。
words.en: Something that is hazardous is dangerous, especially to people's health or safety.

words.ex: The city was covered in haze this morning.
words.ex_cn: 今天早上这座城市被雾霾笼罩。
words.en: Haze is a light mist or fog, especially one caused by the heat of the sun or by pollution.

words.tr:
adv. 头向前地；倒栽葱地；急速地；鲁莽地
adj. 头向前的；倒栽葱的；急速的；急骤的
words.ex: He jumped headlong into the pool.
words.ex_cn: 他头向前地跳进了泳池。
words.en: If you move headlong in a particular direction, you move there very quickly and without thinking carefully about what you are doing.

words.tr: adj. 刚愎自用的；顽固的；任性的
words.ex: He is headstrong and refuses to listen.
words.ex_cn: 他很固执，不肯听别人的话。
words.en: If you refer to someone as headstrong, you are slightly critical of them because they are very determined to do what they want, and refuse to be advised by others.

words.ex: He will hearken to his teacher's advice.
words.ex_cn: 他会听从老师的建议。
words.en: To listen attentively or give heed to something or someone.

words.tr: n. 传闻；谣传；道听途说
words.ex: He believed the hearsay without checking the facts.
words.ex_cn: 他没有核实事实就相信了这些流言。
words.en: Information received from other people that one cannot adequately substantiate; rumor.

words.ex: Her smile heartened the tired students.
words.ex_cn: 她的微笑鼓舞了疲惫的学生。
words.en: If someone is heartened by something, it encourages them and makes them cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 使人悲痛的；令人心碎的
words.ex: The story of the orphan's struggle was heartrending.
words.ex_cn: 这个孤儿奋斗的故事令人心碎。
words.en: Causing great sadness or distress.

words.ex: His views were considered heretical by the religious authorities.
words.ex_cn: 他的观点被宗教权威认为是异端的。
words.en: If someone's beliefs or actions are heretical, they are contrary to the official or accepted beliefs or practices of a particular religion or group.

words.tr: n. 隐士；隐居者；遁世者
words.ex: The hermit lives alone in a small cave.
words.ex_cn: 这位隐士独自住在一个小山洞里。
words.en: A hermit is someone who lives alone and apart from society, often for religious reasons.

words.ex: His heterodox ideas shocked the traditional scholars.
words.ex_cn: 他的非正统观点让传统学者感到震惊。
words.en: Heterodox ideas, opinions, or practices are different from the accepted or official ones.

words.tr: adj. 异种的；异质的；由不同成份形成的
words.ex: The class is heterogeneous, with students from many countries.
words.ex_cn: 这个班级是多元的，有来自许多国家的学生。
words.en: A heterogeneous group consists of many different types of things or people.

words.ex: That park was in its heyday in the 1990s.
words.ex_cn: 那个公园在20世纪90年代是它的鼎盛时期。
words.en: The period of a person's or thing's greatest success, popularity, or vigor.

words.tr: adj. 丑恶的；可怕的；丑陋的；
words.ex: The monster had a hideous face.
words.ex_cn: 这个怪物有一张丑恶的脸。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is hideous, you mean that they are very ugly or unattractive.

words.tr: n. 层次体系；等级制度；
words.ex: The company has a clear hierarchy from manager to worker.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司有一个从经理到员工的明确层次体系。
words.en: A hierarchy is a system in which people or things are arranged according to their importance.

words.ex: Rain can hinder our plan to go hiking.
words.ex_cn: 雨天会妨碍我们去徒步旅行的计划。
words.en: If something hinders you, it makes it more difficult for you to do something or make progress.

words.ex: With hindsight, I should have saved more money.
words.ex_cn: 事后看来，我本该多存些钱。
words.en: The understanding of a situation or event only after it has happened or developed.

words.ex: Hitherto, no one has solved the problem.
words.ex_cn: 迄今为止，没有人解决过这个问题。
words.en: Until now or until the point in time under discussion.

words.tr:
n. 贮藏物；隐藏物
v. 贮藏；囤积
words.ex: The treasure hunter found a hoard of gold coins.
words.ex_cn: 寻宝者发现了一堆金币。
words.en: If you hoard things such as food or money, you save or store them, often in secret, because they are valuable or important to you.

words.tr:
n. 骗局；恶作剧；戏弄
v. 愚弄
words.ex: The news was a hoax to scare people.
words.ex_cn: 这则新闻是个骗局，为了吓唬人。
words.en: A hoax is a plan to deceive someone, such as telling the police there is a bomb somewhere when there is not, or a trick in which someone tells people a lie.

words.tr: v. 跛行；蹒跚；捆绑（马等的）两腿
words.ex: The old man hobbled along the street.
words.ex_cn: 那位老人一瘸一拐地走在街上。
words.en: If you hobble, you walk in an awkward way, usually because your feet or legs hurt.

words.ex: The drawer was a hodgepodge of old keys, buttons, and papers.
words.ex_cn: 抽屉里堆满了旧钥匙、纽扣和纸张的混杂物。
words.en: A hodgepodge is a confused mixture of different things.

words.tr:
n. 电话；
v. 打电话；
words.ex: I lost my phone yesterday.
words.ex_cn: 我昨天丢了电话。
words.en: A phone is a piece of equipment that you use to talk to someone who is in another place.

words.tr:
n. 猎犬
v. 追逐；纠缠
words.ex: The hound chased the rabbit through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 猎犬在森林里追赶兔子。
words.en: A hound is a type of dog used for hunting or chasing. It can also refer to someone who persistently pursues or bothers someone else.

words.ex: The bird hovers above the flowers.
words.ex_cn: 鸟在花上空盘旋。
words.en: To remain in one place in the air, or to stay close to someone or something.

words.ex: The hubbub in the market made it hard to think.
words.ex_cn: 市场里的喧闹让人难以集中思想。
words.en: A hubbub is a loud, confused noise, especially one caused by a large crowd of people.

words.ex: His hubris made him lose the game.
words.ex_cn: 他的傲慢让他输掉了比赛。
words.en: Hubris is excessive pride or self-confidence, often leading to downfall or failure.

words.tr: n. 大型废弃物；巨大笨重的人（物）
words.ex: The old boat was left as a hulk on the shore.
words.ex_cn: 那艘旧船被遗弃在岸边，成为了一堆大型废弃物。
words.en: A hulk is a large, clumsy, or old ship that is no longer in use and is often left to decay in a harbor.

words.ex: His daily routine is humdrum.
words.ex_cn: 他的日常生活很单调。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as humdrum, you mean that they are ordinary, dull, or boring.

words.ex: The cat hunched its back when it saw the dog.
words.ex_cn: 猫看到狗时，背部拱了起来。
words.en: A hunch is a feeling or guess based on intuition rather than known facts.

words.tr: adj. 催眠的；引起睡眠的；
words.ex: The soft music had a hypnotic effect.
words.ex_cn: 柔和的音乐有催眠效果。
words.en: Something that is hypnotic holds your attention or makes you feel very relaxed, often in a way that is similar to being hypnotized.

words.ex: He is a hypocrite because he says he loves peace but fights often.
words.ex_cn: 他是个伪君子，因为他声称热爱和平，却经常打架。
words.en: A hypocrite is someone who pretends to have certain beliefs or opinions that they do not really have, especially in order to deceive people.

words.ex: His idiosyncrasy is talking to himself while reading.
words.ex_cn: 他的怪癖是读书时自言自语。
words.en: An idiosyncrasy is a peculiar or unusual habit, way of behaving, or feature that someone or something has.

words.tr:
v. 无所事事；闲荡
adj. 懈怠的；闲散的；不做事的
words.ex: He idles away the whole afternoon.
words.ex_cn: 他整个下午都无所事事。
words.en: If you describe someone as idle, you mean they are not doing anything or they are not working hard.

words.tr: n. 耻辱；屈辱；名誉受损
words.ex: He faced ignominy after lying to the court.
words.ex_cn: 他在法庭上撒谎后遭到了耻辱。
words.en: Ignominy is a situation or event that causes you to feel ashamed or embarrassed, especially when this is public.

words.tr: adj. 粗野的；无教养的；教养不好的
words.ex: His ill-bred comments offended many people.
words.ex_cn: 他粗野的评论冒犯了许多人的。
words.en: If you describe someone as ill-bred, you mean that they have bad manners because their parents did not teach them how to behave properly.

words.ex: His handwriting is illegible.
words.ex_cn: 他的字迹无法辨认。
words.en: If something is illegible, it is impossible to read because the letters or characters are not clear, are not formed properly, or are obscured in some way.

words.ex: He is an illustrious scientist who won many awards.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位杰出的科学家，获得过许多奖项。
words.en: If you describe someone as illustrious, you mean that they are very well known because they have a high position in society or they have done something impressive.

words.ex: The teacher imbues her students with confidence.
words.ex_cn: 老师赋予学生信心。
words.en: If someone or something is imbued with a particular quality, feeling, or value, they are filled with it or characterized by it.

words.tr: adj. 内在的；无所不在的
words.ex: The immanent laws of nature govern all living things.
words.ex_cn: 自然界的内在法则支配着所有生物。
words.en: Existing or operating within; inherent.

words.ex: The injury impaired his ability to walk.
words.ex_cn: 这次受伤损害了他走路的能力。
words.en: If something impairs something such as an ability or the way something works, it damages it or makes it worse.

words.ex: He imparts knowledge to his students every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天向学生传授知识。
words.en: If you impart information to people, you tell it to them. To impart a particular quality to something means to give it that quality.

words.ex: The president may be impeached for lying.
words.ex_cn: 总统可能因撒谎而被弹劾。
words.en: If a government official is impeached, they are formally charged with a serious crime in a special government court.

words.tr: adj. 无可挑剔的；无瑕疵的；
words.ex: Her impeccable manners impressed everyone at the dinner.
words.ex_cn: 她无可挑剔的礼仪让晚宴上的每个人都印象深刻。
words.en: If you describe something as impeccable, you are emphasizing that it is perfect and has no faults.

words.ex: The fallen tree impeded the car's path.
words.ex_cn: 倒下的树阻碍了汽车的前进。
words.en: To impede something means to make its movement, development, or progress difficult.

words.tr:
adj. 极重要的；
n. 紧急的事；
words.ex: It is imperative to drink water every day.
words.ex_cn: 每天喝水非常重要。
words.en: If it is imperative that something is done, that thing is extremely important and must be done.

words.ex: The imperial palace was built long ago.
words.ex_cn: 这座帝国宫殿是很久以前建造的。
words.en: relating to an empire or an emperor; majestic or superior in quality or size

words.ex: Smoking can imperil your health.
words.ex_cn: 吸烟会危及你的健康。
words.en: To put someone or something at risk of being harmed, damaged, or destroyed.

words.ex: The imperious queen demanded immediate obedience.
words.ex_cn: 这位专横的女王要求立即服从。
words.en: If you describe someone as imperious, you mean that they have a proud manner and expect to be obeyed.

words.tr: adj. 不能渗透的；不受影响的
words.ex: The coat is impervious to rain.
words.ex_cn: 这件外套不透水。
words.en: If you are impervious to someone's actions, you are not affected or influenced by them.

words.ex: He made an impetuous decision to quit his job.
words.ex_cn: 他冲动地决定辞去工作。
words.en: If you describe someone as impetuous, you mean that they are likely to act quickly and suddenly without thinking or being careful.

words.ex: The new law gave impetus to environmental protection.
words.ex_cn: 新法律为环境保护提供了推动力。
words.en: Something that gives a process impetus or an impetus makes it happen or progress more quickly.

words.tr: n. 冒名顶替者；冒名行骗者
words.ex: She felt like an imposter in her own life.
words.ex_cn: 她觉得自己在生活中像个冒名顶替者。
words.en: An imposter is someone who pretends to be someone else in order to deceive others, especially for fraudulent gain.

words.ex: The war impoverished many families.
words.ex_cn: 这场战争使许多家庭变得贫困。
words.en: To make someone poor or to reduce the quality, strength, or richness of something.

words.tr: v. 即兴创作；即兴表演；临时准备；
words.ex: He improvise a song on the piano.
words.ex_cn: 他即兴创作了一首钢琴曲。
words.en: If you improvise, you make or do something using whatever you have or without having planned it in advance.

words.ex: He made an imprudent decision and lost all his money.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个鲁莽的决定，失去了所有钱。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour as imprudent, you think it is not sensible or carefully thought out.

words.tr: adj. 鲁莽的；厚颜的；冒失的；放肆无礼的
words.ex: The impudent boy talked back to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 这个鲁莽的男孩顶撞了老师。
words.en: If you describe someone as impudent, you mean they are rude or disrespectful, or they show a lack of shame about their behavior.

words.ex: He will impugn the witness's honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他将质疑证人的诚实性。
words.en: To impugn means to challenge as false or questionable; to cast doubt upon.

words.tr: adj. 愚蠢的；空洞的；无意义的
words.ex: His inane comments made everyone bored.
words.ex_cn: 他无聊的评论让每个人都感到无聊。
words.en: If you describe someone's comments or ideas as inane, you mean they are very silly or stupid.

words.tr: v. （人、动物）（尤指多代）近亲繁殖
words.ex: Inbreeding can lead to genetic defects.
words.ex_cn: 近亲繁殖可能导致遗传缺陷。
words.en: To breed from closely related individuals, especially over many generations.

words.tr:
n. 熏香；熏香的烟
v. 使愤怒；激怒
words.ex: The smell of incense fills the room.
words.ex_cn: 香火的气味充满了房间。
words.en: Incense is a substance that is burned for its pleasant smell, often used in religious ceremonies. As a verb, to incense means to make someone very angry.

words.ex: The project began at its inception.
words.ex_cn: 这个项目从开始时就启动了。
words.en: The inception of something is the start or beginning of it.

words.tr: adj. 初始的；早期的；未形成的
words.ex: His idea was still inchoate.
words.ex_cn: 他的想法还很不成熟。
words.en: If something is inchoate, it is just beginning to form or is not fully developed or clear.

words.ex: The incipient fire was put out quickly.
words.ex_cn: 初期的小火被迅速扑灭了。
words.en: An incipient situation or quality is one that is just beginning to develop or become noticeable.

words.ex: The weather was inclement, so we stayed home.
words.ex_cn: 天气恶劣，所以我们待在家里。
words.en: (of weather) unpleasantly cold or wet.

words.tr:
adj. 不可挽救的；屡教不改的；不可救药的
n. 无可救药的人
words.ex: He is an incorrigible liar.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个无可救药的骗子。
words.en: If you describe someone as incorrigible, you mean that they have faults which they seem unable or unwilling to correct, even though they are aware of them.

words.ex: The hen incubate eggs until they hatch.
words.ex_cn: 母鸡孵化鸡蛋直到小鸡孵出。
words.en: to keep eggs warm so that they develop and hatch, or to keep cells, bacteria, etc. at a suitable temperature so that they develop

words.tr: v. 反复灌输；谆谆劝导
words.ex: Parents try to inculcate good habits in their children.
words.ex_cn: 父母试图在孩子身上培养良好的习惯。
words.en: To inculcate is to teach and impress by frequent repetitions or admonitions.

words.ex: He incurred a fine for speeding.
words.ex_cn: 他因超速而招致了一笔罚款。
words.en: If you incur something unpleasant, it happens to you because of something you have done.

words.ex: He is indebted to the bank for a large loan.
words.ex_cn: 他欠银行一大笔贷款。
words.en: If you say that you are indebted to someone for something, you mean that you are very grateful to them for something.

words.ex: The company paid indemnity for the damaged car.
words.ex_cn: 公司为损坏的汽车支付了保险赔偿。
words.en: If something provides indemnity, it provides insurance or protection against damage or loss, especially in the form of a legal agreement.

words.tr: n. 指标；索引；指数；“index”的复数
words.ex: The company tracks key indices to measure performance.
words.ex_cn: 该公司追踪关键指标以衡量表现。
words.en: Indices are used to measure or indicate something, such as economic health or the performance of a stock market.

words.ex: The court will indict him for theft.
words.ex_cn: 法院将对他提起盗窃指控。
words.en: If someone is indicted for a crime, they are officially charged with it.

words.ex: He lived in indigence after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后生活贫困。
words.en: Indigence is the state of being extremely poor.

words.ex: The indigenous people live in the forest.
words.ex_cn: 本土居民住在森林里。
words.en: Indigenous people or things belong to the country in which they are found, rather than coming there or being brought there from another country.

words.ex: They tried to indoctrinate the children with their beliefs.
words.ex_cn: 他们试图用他们的信仰灌输孩子们。
words.en: To indoctrinate someone means to teach them a particular belief or set of beliefs, especially with the aim of making them accept it without questioning it.

words.ex: His indolence at work was becoming a serious issue.
words.ex_cn: 他在工作中的懒散正成为一个严重的问题。
words.en: Indolence is the state of being lazy or not wanting to do any work.

words.tr: adj. 不屈不挠的；百折不挠的
words.ex: He is indomitable in facing challenges.
words.ex_cn: 他在面对挑战时永不言败。
words.en: If you say that someone has an indomitable spirit, you admire them because they never give up or admit that they have been defeated.

words.ex: His genius is indubitable.
words.ex_cn: 他的天才是不容置疑的。
words.en: If you describe something as indubitable, you mean that it is definitely true.

words.ex: He is an industrious student who studies every day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个勤勉的学生，每天都学习。
words.en: Someone who is industrious works hard and is determined.

words.tr: adj. 不可言喻的；无法形容的；避讳的
words.ex: The beauty of the sunset was ineffable.
words.ex_cn: 日落的美是无法言喻的。
words.en: If you describe something as ineffable, you mean that it is so impressive or extreme that it cannot be described in words.

words.tr: adj. 不可避免的；必然发生的
words.ex: The outcome was ineluctable.
words.ex_cn: 结果是不可避免的。
words.en: Something that is ineluctable cannot be avoided or escaped from.

words.ex: The inert gas does not react with other elements.
words.ex_cn: 这种惰性气体不与其他元素发生反应。
words.en: If someone or something is inert, they are not moving or reacting in any way.

words.ex: The inexorable flow of time cannot be stopped.
words.ex_cn: 时间不可阻挡地流逝。
words.en: If you describe something as inexorable, you mean that it is impossible to stop or prevent from happening.

words.tr: adj. 无法摆脱的；纠缠的；分不开的
words.ex: Their problems are inextricable.
words.ex_cn: 他们的问题无法分开。
words.en: If you say that something is inextricable from something else, you mean that the two things cannot be considered separately.

words.tr: adj. 婴儿的；幼稚的；孩子气的
words.ex: The infantile smile made everyone feel warm.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿般的微笑让每个人都感到温暖。
words.en: Infantile behavior or illnesses are typical of very young children.

words.ex: Her infatuation with the movie star lasted only a few weeks.
words.ex_cn: 她对那位电影明星的迷恋只持续了几个星期。
words.en: An infatuation is an intense but short-lived passion or admiration for someone or something.

words.tr: n. 地狱；炼狱；无法控制的大火
words.ex: The city was an inferno of fire and destruction.
words.ex_cn: 这座城市成了火与毁灭的地狱。
words.en: An inferno is a place or situation that is extremely hot and fiery, resembling hell.

words.tr: v. 大批出没于；成群滋扰；遍布于；寄生
words.ex: The bugs infest the old house.
words.ex_cn: 这些虫子侵袭了这栋老房子。
words.en: If creatures such as insects or rats infest a place, they are present in large numbers and usually cause damage or disease.

words.ex: The company is suffering from severe infighting among senior executives.
words.ex_cn: 公司正遭受高层管理人员之间的严重内斗。
words.en: Infighting refers to conflict or competition between members of the same group or organization, often leading to a negative impact on the group's effectiveness or cohesion.

words.ex: The difference between the two values is infinitesimal.
words.ex_cn: 这两个值之间的差异极微。
words.en: Something that is infinitesimal is extremely small.

words.tr: v. 膨胀；使充气；夸口；吹嘘
words.ex: He tries to inflate the balloon with his mouth.
words.ex_cn: 他试图用嘴把气球吹大。
words.en: To inflate something means to cause it to increase in size by filling it with air or gas. It can also refer to increasing the amount of money in circulation, leading to a decrease in its value.

words.tr: vt. 弯曲；改变；使屈曲; vi. 发生曲折变化
words.ex: The wind inflects the tree branches.
words.ex_cn: 风使树枝弯曲。
words.en: To change the form of a word to express a different grammatical function or attribute; to alter the pitch or tone of the voice.

words.ex: There was a large influx of tourists during the summer.
words.ex_cn: 夏天期间涌入了大量游客。
words.en: An influx of people or things is a large number of them arriving somewhere at the same time.

words.ex: He got a fine for a small infraction.
words.ex_cn: 他因一个小违规行为被罚款。
words.en: An infraction is a violation or infringement of a law, agreement, or set of rules.

words.ex: He infringes the rules by arriving late.
words.ex_cn: 他因迟到而违反了规则。
words.en: To infringe means to violate or break a law, agreement, or right.

words.ex: The noise infuriates my neighbor.
words.ex_cn: 噪音让我的邻居非常生气。
words.en: To make someone extremely angry.

words.tr: adj. 单纯的；天真的；坦率的
words.ex: He gave an ingenuous smile when he told the truth.
words.ex_cn: 当他讲真话时，他露出了天真无邪的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as ingenuous, you mean that they are innocent, trusting, and honest, often in a way that seems naive.

words.ex: The baby ingests milk every few hours.
words.ex_cn: 婴儿每隔几小时喝奶。
words.en: To ingest means to take food, drink, or another substance into your body, usually by swallowing.

words.ex: He was an ingrate who never thanked anyone for their help.
words.ex_cn: 他是个忘恩负义的人，从不感谢别人的帮助。
words.en: An ingrate is a person who is not grateful for something that has been done for them.

words.ex: The company's policies were inimical to the interests of its employees.
words.ex_cn: 公司的政策对员工的利益是有害的。
words.en: If one thing is inimical to another, it prevents the second thing from happening or being successful, or it is harmful to it.

words.tr: adj. 无害的；无冒犯之意的
words.ex: The comment was innocuous and didn't upset anyone.
words.ex_cn: 这个评论无害，没有惹恼任何人。
words.en: Something that is innocuous is not harmful or offensive.

words.ex: He spent inordinate time on video games.
words.ex_cn: 他花了过多的时间玩电子游戏。
words.en: If you describe something as inordinate, you are emphasizing that it is unusually or excessively large in amount or degree.

words.tr: adj. 阴险的；潜伏的；暗中作祟的
words.ex: The insidious virus spread quietly through the town.
words.ex_cn: 这种隐蔽的病毒悄然在小镇蔓延。
words.en: Proceeding in a gradual, subtle way, but with harmful effects.

words.ex: He insinuated that she was lying.
words.ex_cn: 他暗示她在撒谎。
words.en: If you say that someone insinuates that something bad is the case, you mean that they say it in an indirect way.

words.tr: adj. 淡而无味的；枯燥乏味的
words.ex: The soup was insipid and boring.
words.ex_cn: 这汤淡而无味，很无聊。
words.en: If you describe food or drink as insipid, you mean that it is very weak, tasteless, or uninteresting.

words.tr: adj. 傲慢的；无礼的；侮慢的
words.ex: The insolent boy talked back to his teacher.
words.ex_cn: 那个无礼的男孩顶撞了老师。
words.en: If you say that someone is insolent, you mean they are rude and do not show respect for people in positions of authority.

words.tr: adj. 海岛的；孤立的；思想褊狭的
words.ex: The insular village has no bridge to the mainland.
words.ex_cn: 这个海岛村庄没有桥通向大陆。
words.en: If you describe someone as insular, you are being critical of them because they are unwilling to meet new people or to consider new ideas.

words.tr: v. 隔离；使隔热；使隔音；使绝缘
words.ex: The walls insulate the house from cold air.
words.ex_cn: 墙壁将房子与冷空气隔离开。
words.en: To insulate something means to protect it from heat, cold, noise, or electricity by covering it in a material that prevents it from passing through.

words.ex: The language barrier was insuperable for him.
words.ex_cn: 语言障碍对他来说是难以克服的。
words.en: If you describe a problem or obstacle as insuperable, you mean that it is impossible to overcome.

words.tr: adj. 无法克服的；难以解决的；不可逾越的
words.ex: The problem seemed insurmountable.
words.ex_cn: 这个问题似乎无法克服。
words.en: If you describe something as insurmountable, you mean that it is so great or severe that it cannot be dealt with.

words.ex: He will intercede for his friend.
words.ex_cn: 他会为他的朋友出面说情。
words.en: If you intercede with someone, you try to persuade them to forgive someone or end their disagreement with them.

words.tr:
n. （法庭的）禁令；禁止
v. 禁止（行动）；阻断
words.ex: The court issued an interdict to stop the construction.
words.ex_cn: 法院发布了一项禁令，以停止施工。
words.en: If someone is interdicted from doing something, they are officially prevented from doing it by a law or a rule.

words.tr: adj. 断断续续的；间歇的
words.ex: The rain is intermittent today.
words.ex_cn: 今天雨断断续续地下。
words.en: Something that is intermittent happens occasionally rather than continuously.

words.ex: The historian interpolated the text with his own opinions.
words.ex_cn: 这位历史学家在文本中插入了自己的观点。
words.en: To interpolate means to insert something between other things or parts, especially to insert words into a text.

words.ex: The bully tried to intimidate the new student.
words.ex_cn: 那个霸凌者试图恐吓新生。
words.en: If you intimidate someone, you deliberately make them frightened enough to do what you want them to do.

words.tr:
adj. 醉人的
n. 酒精饮料；致醉药物
words.ex: Alcohol is a common intoxicant.
words.ex_cn: 酒精是一种常见的致醉物。
words.en: An intoxicant is a substance that can cause intoxication, such as alcohol or drugs.

words.ex: The lock has an intricate design.
words.ex_cn: 这个锁有复杂的结构。
words.en: You use intricate to describe something that has many small parts or details.

words.ex: He tries to introspect about his mistakes.
words.ex_cn: 他试图反省自己的错误。
words.en: If you introspect, you examine your own ideas, thoughts, and feelings.

words.ex: He inured himself to the cold weather.
words.ex_cn: 他让自己适应了寒冷的天气。
words.en: If you are inured to something unpleasant, you have become used to it so that it no longer affects you.

words.ex: The store made an inventory of all the products.
words.ex_cn: 商店对所有商品做了一份清单。
words.en: An inventory is a detailed list of all the items in a place.

words.tr: adj. 根深蒂固的；积习难改的
words.ex: He is an inveterate smoker who cannot quit.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个根深蒂固的吸烟者，无法戒掉。
words.en: If you describe someone as, for example, an inveterate liar or smoker, you mean that they have lied or smoked for a long time and are not likely to stop doing it.

words.tr: adj. 招致不满的；不公平的；难以决定的
words.ex: He made an invidious comparison between his two students.
words.ex_cn: 他对他的两个学生做了令人不快的比较。
words.en: If you describe a task or job as invidious, you mean that it is likely to make you unpopular because it is unpleasant or difficult to do.

words.tr: adj. 不可征服的；不能战胜的
words.ex: He felt invincible after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 赢得比赛后，他觉得自己不可战胜。
words.en: If someone or something is invincible, they are impossible to defeat or overcome.

words.tr: adj. 不容亵渎的；不可侵犯的
words.ex: Her privacy is inviolable.
words.ex_cn: 她的隐私是不可侵犯的。
words.en: If a law or principle is inviolable, it must not be broken or treated without respect.

words.ex: He invoked the law to protect his rights.
words.ex_cn: 他援引法律来保护自己的权利。
words.en: If you invoke a law, rule, or principle, you refer to it as a reason or justification for something.

words.ex: He is irascible when he wakes up late.
words.ex_cn: 他起床晚时容易发怒。
words.en: If you describe someone as irascible, you mean that they become angry very easily.

words.tr: adj. 彩虹色的；色彩斑斓的
words.ex: The soap bubble is iridescent in the sunlight.
words.ex_cn: 肥皂泡在阳光下呈现出彩虹色。
words.en: Showing luminous colors that seem to change when seen from different angles.

words.tr: v. 使恼怒；使厌烦；使烦恼
words.ex: The loud noise irks her every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上，巨大的噪音都让她感到烦躁。
words.en: To irritate, annoy, or exasperate someone.

words.tr: v. 激怒；使急躁；使疼痛
words.ex: Loud noises irritate my baby.
words.ex_cn: 噪音会激怒我的宝宝。
words.en: If something irritates you, it keeps annoying you.

words.ex: He iterate the importance of honesty.
words.ex_cn: 他反复说诚实的重要性。
words.en: To say or do something again or several times.

words.tr:
adj. 巡回的；流动的
n. 四处奔波的人；流浪者
words.ex: The itinerant worker moves from town to town for jobs.
words.ex_cn: 这位流动工人为了工作从一个城镇搬到另一个城镇。
words.en: Someone who is itinerant travels from place to place, usually because they have no permanent home or job, or because they are involved in a particular activity that requires this.

words.ex: We planned our itinerary before the trip.
words.ex_cn: 我们在旅行前规划了路线。
words.en: An itinerary is a plan of a journey, including the route and the places that you will visit.

words.tr: adj. 精疲力竭的；腻烦的；无兴致的
words.ex: She felt jaded after a long day at work.
words.ex_cn: 工作了一整天后，她感到精疲力竭。
words.en: If you are jaded, you feel bored, tired, and not enthusiastic, especially because you have had too much of something.

words.ex: Don't jeopardize your health by skipping meals.
words.ex_cn: 不要因为不吃饭而危及你的健康。
words.en: To jeopardize something means to do something that may destroy it or cause it to be lost.

words.tr: n.  沙文主义者；侵略主义者
words.ex: He was criticized for his jingoist views on foreign policy.
words.ex_cn: 他因在外交政策上的沙文主义观点而受到批评。
words.en: A jingoist is someone who believes that their own country is always best and who is in favor of aggressive or warlike policies towards other countries.

words.tr: adj. 诙谐的；爱开玩笑的；滑稽的
words.ex: He is jocular during breaks, making everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他在休息时很幽默，让大家笑个不停。
words.en: If you say that someone has a jocular manner, you mean that they are cheerful and often make jokes or try to make people laugh.

words.tr: adj.  快活的；愉快的；高兴的
words.ex: His jovial nature made him popular among his colleagues.
words.ex_cn: 他天性快活，这使他在同事中很受欢迎。
words.en: If you describe someone as jovial, you mean that they are happy and cheerful.

words.tr: adj. 欢腾的；欢欣鼓舞的
words.ex: The children were jubilant after winning the game.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们赢了比赛后非常高兴。
words.en: If you are jubilant, you feel extremely happy because of a success.

words.tr: adj. 明智的；有见识的；判断正确的
words.ex: He made a judicious choice about which book to buy.
words.ex_cn: 他做出了一个明智的买书决定。
words.en: If you describe an action or decision as judicious, you approve of it because you think that it shows good judgment and sense.

words.ex: She tries to juggle her job and caring for her kids.
words.ex_cn: 她努力兼顾工作和照顾孩子。
words.en: If you juggle, you keep several objects in motion in the air at the same time by repeatedly throwing and catching them. Juggle can also mean to deal with several things at the same time, often in a skillful way.

words.tr:
v. 使混乱；使杂乱
n. 杂乱；混乱
words.ex: He jumbled the letters and could not read the word.
words.ex_cn: 他把字母弄乱了，无法认出这个单词。
words.en: To mix things together in a confused or untidy way.

words.ex: The car stopped at the junction.
words.ex_cn: 汽车在交叉路口停了下来。
words.en: A junction is a place where two or more things, especially roads or railways, come together.

words.ex: At this juncture, we need to make a decision.
words.ex_cn: 在这一关键时刻，我们需要做出决定。
words.en: A particular point in events or time, especially one that is critical or decisive.

words.tr: n. 扫兴的人；煞风景的人
words.ex: She was a killjoy, always finding something to complain about.
words.ex_cn: 她是个令人扫兴的人，总是能找到抱怨的事情。
words.en: A killjoy is someone who spoils other people's fun or enjoyment.

words.tr:
n. 亲属；血缘关系
adj. 同源的；类似的
words.ex: He visited his kindred during the holiday.
words.ex_cn: 他在假期里探望了他的亲属。
words.en: If two people or things are kindred, they are similar in some way, often because they are related.

words.ex: He has a knack for fixing bikes.
words.ex_cn: 他有修自行车的技巧。
words.en: A knack is a special skill or ability that someone has, especially one that is hard to explain or teach.

words.ex: She knit a warm scarf for her brother.
words.ex_cn: 她为她的弟弟织了一条暖和的围巾。
words.en: If you knit something, especially an article of clothing, you make it from wool or a similar thread by using two knitting needles or a machine.

words.tr: adj. 无光泽的；暗淡的；无生气的；乏善可陈的
words.ex: The paint on the car looked lackluster after the storm.
words.ex_cn: 这场风暴过后，车漆显得暗淡无光。
words.en: If you describe something as lackluster, you mean that it is not exciting or not very good quality.

words.tr: adj. 言简意赅的；简明扼要的；凝练的
words.ex: He gave a laconic reply: 'Yes.'
words.ex_cn: 他简短地回答：‘是的。’
words.en: If you describe someone as laconic, you mean that they use very few words to say something, so that they seem casual or unfriendly.

words.ex: He was always the laggard in the race.
words.ex_cn: 在比赛中他总是落后者。
words.en: A laggard is someone who is very slow to do something or to make progress.

words.ex: She lamented the death of her dog.
words.ex_cn: 她哀悼她狗的去世。
words.en: If you lament something, you express your sadness, regret, or disappointment about it.

words.tr: adj. 无精打采的；疲倦无力的
words.ex: He gave a languid smile before lying down.
words.ex_cn: 他躺下前给了一个慵懒的微笑。
words.en: If you describe someone as languid, you mean that they show little energy or interest and are very slow and casual in their movements.

words.tr:
n. 倒塌；崩溃；暴跌；
v. 倒塌；崩溃；
words.ex: The collapse of the old bridge caused many problems.
words.ex_cn: 这座旧桥的倒塌引起了诸多问题。
words.en: If a building or other structure collapses, it falls down very suddenly.

words.tr: n. 赏赐；赠品；贺礼；慷慨赠与的钱或物
words.ex: The king showed largesse to the poor people.
words.ex_cn: 国王向穷人施舍恩惠。
words.en: Generosity in bestowing money or gifts upon others.

words.ex: The latent talent in the child became clear after years of practice.
words.ex_cn: 孩子潜在的才能在多年练习后显现出来。
words.en: Latent is used to describe something which is hidden and not obvious at the moment, but which may develop further in the future.

words.ex: The car made a lateral move to avoid the dog.
words.ex_cn: 汽车横向移动以避开狗。
words.en: Relating to the side or sides; situated at or extending to the side.

words.tr: adj. 松弛的；懒散的；马虎的
words.ex: He is lax about his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他对作业很松懈。
words.en: If you say that a person's behaviour or a system is lax, you mean they are not careful or strict about maintaining high standards.

words.ex: The doctor explained the disease in layman terms.
words.ex_cn: 医生用通俗易懂的语言解释了这种疾病。
words.en: A layman is a person who does not have specialized or professional knowledge of a subject.

words.tr: n. 牵狗的链子或皮带；控制；约束
words.ex: He holds the dog's leash tightly.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧握着狗的牵引绳。
words.en: A leash is a rope or a strap that you attach to a dog's collar so that you can control the dog.

words.tr: adj. 猜疑的；机警的；有戒心的
words.ex: He was leery of strangers and preferred to keep to himself.
words.ex_cn: 他对陌生人很猜疑，宁愿独来独往。
words.en: If you are leery of something or someone, you are cautious or suspicious about them.

words.tr: adj. 宽厚的；仁慈的；不严格的；
words.ex: The teacher was lenient with students who were late.
words.ex_cn: 老师对迟到的学生很宽厚。
words.en: If you are lenient with someone, you are not strict in the way you treat them, especially when they have done something wrong.

words.tr: n. 损害；身体上的伤害
words.ex: The doctor found a lesion on his skin.
words.ex_cn: 医生在他的皮肤上发现了一个病灶。
words.en: A lesion is an area of damage to the body, such as a wound, ulcer, or tumor.

words.ex: He felt lethargy after eating too much junk food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃完太多垃圾食品后感到无精打采。
words.en: Lethargy is the condition or state of being lethargic; sluggishness, drowsiness, or apathy.

words.tr: adj. 头脑冷静的；清醒的
words.ex: She is always levelheaded in a crisis.
words.ex_cn: 她在危机中总是保持冷静。
words.en: If you describe a person as levelheaded, you mean that they are calm and sensible even in difficult situations.

words.tr:
v. 征收；征税；征募
n. 征兵；征税
words.ex: The government will levy a new tax next month.
words.ex_cn: 政府下个月将征收一项新税。
words.en: To levy means to impose or collect a tax, fee, or fine. It can also refer to the act of enlisting or drafting individuals into military service.

words.ex: He gave an explicit answer to the question.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个问题给出了明确的答案。
words.en: Something that is explicit is expressed or shown clearly and openly, without any attempt to hide anything.

words.tr:
adj. 柔软的；可塑的；易弯曲的；有弹性的
v. 使柔软；把（火炮）系在前车上；做热身运动
n. （拖炮车的）前车
words.ex: The gymnast's body is remarkably limber.
words.ex_cn: 这位体操运动员的身体非常柔软。
words.en: Capable of moving or bending easily; flexible.

words.tr: adj. 清澈的；透明的；清晰的
words.ex: The lake water is limpid and clear.
words.ex_cn: 湖水清澈透明。
words.en: Clear and transparent, especially in a way that makes it easy to understand.

words.ex: He traced his lineage back to ancient kings.
words.ex_cn: 他追溯了自己的家系到古代的国王。
words.en: Your lineage is the series of families from which you are directly descended.

words.ex: He lingered by the door, not wanting to leave.
words.ex_cn: 他逗留在门口，不想离开。
words.en: If you linger somewhere, you stay there for a longer time than is necessary, for example because you are enjoying yourself.

words.ex: Her lissome movements captivated the audience.
words.ex_cn: 她柔软敏捷的动作吸引了观众。
words.en: If you describe someone as lissome, you mean they are thin, supple, and graceful.

words.ex: He felt listless after the long illness.
words.ex_cn: 他生病后感到无精打采。
words.en: If someone is listless, they lack energy or enthusiasm.

words.tr: adj. 易弯的；柔软的；动作轻盈的
words.ex: The dancer is lithe and moves gracefully.
words.ex_cn: 这位舞者身材柔韧，动作优雅。
words.en: A person or animal that is lithe is thin, supple, and graceful.

words.tr: adj. 不乐意的；不情愿的；
words.ex: He is loath to apologize for his mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他不乐意为自己的错误道歉。
words.en: If you are loath to do something, you do not want to do it.

words.ex: I loathe waking up early.
words.ex_cn: 我讨厌早起。
words.en: If you loathe something or someone, you dislike them very much.

words.ex: We waited in the hotel lobby for our friend.
words.ex_cn: 我们在酒店的大厅里等我们的朋友。
words.en: A lobby is a large room or hall in a building, often used for meetings or as a waiting area. As a verb, to lobby means to try to influence politicians or officials on a particular issue.

words.tr: n. 大笑；笑死我了 (used to express amusement)
words.ex: He told a funny joke and got a big lol.
words.ex_cn: 他讲了个有趣的笑话，引得大家大笑。
words.en: To laugh out loud, especially in response to something humorous.

words.tr:
n. 织布机；
v. 迫近；
words.ex: The old loom made a loud clicking sound.
words.ex_cn: 那台旧织布机发出很大的咔嗒声。
words.en: If something looms over you, it appears as a large or unclear shape, often in a way that is frightening or causes worry.

words.ex: The law has a loophole that lets companies avoid taxes.
words.ex_cn: 这项法律有一个漏洞，让公司可以避税。
words.en: A loophole is a small mistake in a law or set of rules which allows people to do something that would otherwise be illegal or not allowed.

words.tr: adj. 倾向一方的；不平衡的；悬殊的
words.ex: The game was lopsided, and one team won by 10 points.
words.ex_cn: 这场比赛比分悬殊，一支队伍以10分获胜。
words.en: Something that is lopsided is uneven because one side is lower or heavier than the other.

words.tr: adj. 话多的；健谈的；喋喋不休的
words.ex: He is a loquacious man who talks all day.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个整天喋喋不休的人。
words.en: If you describe someone as loquacious, you mean that they talk a lot.

words.ex: The mechanic applied a lubricant to the moving parts.
words.ex_cn: 机械师给活动部件涂上了润滑油。
words.en: A substance, such as oil or grease, used to minimize friction, heat, and wear between mechanical parts in contact with each other.

words.ex: Oil helps to lubricate the engine parts.
words.ex_cn: 油有助于润滑发动机部件。
words.en: To apply a substance such as oil or grease to (something) in order to minimize friction and allow smooth movement.

words.tr: adj. 赚大钱的；获利多的；
words.ex: He took a lucrative job at a tech company.
words.ex_cn: 他去了一家科技公司做一份赚大钱的工作。
words.en: A lucrative activity or job is one that you can earn a lot of money from.

words.tr: adj. 悲哀的；可怜的；郁郁不乐的
words.ex: Her lugubrious expression made everyone feel sad.
words.ex_cn: 她那悲哀的表情让每个人都感到难过。
words.en: If you say that someone or something is lugubrious, you mean that they are sad and solemn.

words.ex: The mother sang a lullaby to her baby.
words.ex_cn: 妈妈为她的宝宝唱了一首摇篮曲。
words.en: A lullaby is a quiet song which is intended to be sung to babies and young children to help them go to sleep.

words.ex: The luminous moon lights up the night.
words.ex_cn: 明亮的月亮照亮了夜晚。
words.en: Something that is luminous shines or glows in the dark.

words.ex: The machinations of the rival company were uncovered.
words.ex_cn: 竞争对手公司的阴谋被揭露了。
words.en: A machination is a plot or scheme, especially one that is complex or devious.

words.tr: adj. 有权威的；地方法官的
words.ex: His magisterial tone left no room for argument.
words.ex_cn: 他那权威的语气让人没有反驳的余地。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or work as magisterial, you mean that they show great authority or ability.

words.tr: adj. 宽宏大量的；有雅量的
words.ex: He was magnanimous and forgave his enemy.
words.ex_cn: 他宽宏大量，原谅了他的敌人。
words.en: If you are magnanimous, you behave kindly and generously toward someone, especially after defeating them or being treated badly by them.

words.tr: n. 巨头；大亨；大资本家
words.ex: The magnate owns many hotels and airlines.
words.ex_cn: 这位大亨拥有许多酒店和航空公司。
words.en: A magnate is a person who is very rich and powerful, especially in a particular industry.

words.tr: n. 支柱；中坚；中流砥柱
words.ex: His support has been the mainstay of the project.
words.ex_cn: 他的支持一直是这个项目的支柱。
words.en: If you describe something as the mainstay of a particular thing, you mean that it is the most basic part of it.

words.tr:
adj. 笨拙的；不机敏的；笨手笨脚的
n. 一个笨拙愚蠢的人
words.ex: He was maladroit when he dropped the glass.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把玻璃杯打翻了。
words.en: If you describe someone as maladroit, you mean that they are clumsy or awkward, especially in social situations.

words.ex: He has a rare malady that doctors are trying to cure.
words.ex_cn: 他患有一种罕见的疾病，医生们正在努力治疗。
words.en: A malady is a disease or illness.

words.tr: n. 身体不适；不快；萎靡不振；痼疾
words.ex: She felt a general malaise after the long flight.
words.ex_cn: 长途飞行后，她感到全身不适。
words.en: A general feeling of discomfort, illness, or unease whose exact cause is difficult to identify.

words.ex: He shouted a malediction at the thief.
words.ex_cn: 他对着小偷咒骂了一句。
words.en: A malediction is a curse or the act of uttering a curse.

words.ex: The police caught the malefactor who stole the money.
words.ex_cn: 警察抓到了偷钱的罪犯。
words.en: A malefactor is someone who has committed a crime or done something wrong.

words.ex: The maleficent storm destroyed many homes.
words.ex_cn: 这场有害的风暴摧毁了许多房屋。
words.en: Causing harm or destruction, especially by supernatural means.

words.ex: He acted out of malice, not mistake.
words.ex_cn: 他是出于恶意，而不是错误。
words.en: Malice is behavior that is intended to harm people or their reputations, or cause them embarrassment and upset.

words.tr:
adj. 有害的；恶意的
v. 中伤；污蔑
words.ex: The virus is malign and spreads quickly.
words.ex_cn: 这种病毒是有害的，并且传播迅速。
words.en: If you malign someone, you say unpleasant and untrue things about them. If something is malign, it is harmful or evil.

words.ex: The clay is malleable and easy to shape.
words.ex_cn: 这种黏土是可塑的，容易塑形。
words.en: If you say that someone is malleable, you mean that they are easily influenced or controlled by other people.

words.tr: n. 狂热； 癖好；躁狂症
words.ex: He has a mania for collecting stamps.
words.ex_cn: 他痴迷于收集邮票。
words.en: An extreme enthusiasm or desire for something, often to the point of obsession.

words.tr: adj. 矫揉造作的；不自然的；守规矩的；彬彬有礼的
words.ex: Her mannered speech was hard to understand.
words.ex_cn: 她矫揉造作的言辞让人难以理解。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior or a work of art as mannered, you dislike it because it is elaborate or formal, and therefore seems false or artificial.

words.ex: The king decided to manumit all the slaves.
words.ex_cn: 国王决定解放所有奴隶。
words.en: To release from slavery or bondage; set free.

words.ex: The stain on the carpet is a mar.
words.ex_cn: 地毯上的污渍是一个污点。
words.en: To mar something means to spoil or damage it.

words.tr: adj. 边缘的；页边的；微不足道的；不重要的
words.ex: The village is on the marginal area of the city.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄位于城市的边缘地区。
words.en: If you describe something as marginal, you mean that it is small or not very important.

words.ex: They are discussing marital problems.
words.ex_cn: 他们正在讨论婚姻问题。
words.en: Marital is used to describe things relating to marriage.

words.ex: He practices martial arts every day.
words.ex_cn: 他每天练习武术。
words.en: Martial is used to describe things relating to soldiers or war.

words.tr: adj. 母亲的；母性的；母系的；
words.ex: Her maternal love kept the family strong.
words.ex_cn: 她的母爱让家庭保持坚强。
words.en: Maternal feelings or actions are typical of a kind, loving mother.

words.ex: The matriarch runs the family with wisdom.
words.ex_cn: 女家长以智慧管理着这个家庭。
words.en: A matriarch is a woman who is the head of a family or tribe.

words.ex: He is a maverick who always does things his own way.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个总是按自己方式做事的独行其是者。
words.en: If you describe someone as a maverick, you mean that they are unconventional and independent, and do not think or behave in the same way as other people.

words.tr:
v. 缓慢而弯曲地流动；漫步；闲聊
n. 河流的曲折；漫步；迂回曲折的进程
words.ex: The river meanders through the forest.
words.ex_cn: 这条河蜿蜒穿过森林。
words.en: To meander means to follow a winding and turning course, often used to describe the way a river flows or the way a person walks without a clear direction.

words.tr: v. 测量；“measure”的过去式和过去分词； adj. 慎重的；谨慎小心的；
words.ex: He measured the length of the table.
words.ex_cn: 他测量了桌子的长度。
words.en: If you describe someone's way of speaking as measured, you mean that it is slow and deliberate, often because they are trying to hide their feelings.

words.tr: v. 沉思；冥想；考虑；仔细计划
words.ex: He meditates every morning to feel calm.
words.ex_cn: 他每天早上冥想以保持平静。
words.en: To meditate means to spend time in quiet thought for religious purposes or relaxation.

words.tr: n. 混杂物；集锦；集成曲
words.ex: The band played a medley of old songs.
words.ex_cn: 乐队演奏了一串老歌的混合曲。
words.en: A medley is a mixture of things, especially a mixture of tunes or songs played one after the other.

words.tr:
n. 忧愁
adj.  忧郁的
words.ex: He felt melancholy after the rain stopped.
words.ex_cn: 雨停后，他感到忧郁。
words.en: A feeling of deep sadness, typically with no obvious cause.

words.tr:
v. （使）合并；（使）融合；（使）混合
n. 合并；混合
words.ex: He melds the two ideas into one.
words.ex_cn: 他把这两个想法融合成一个。
words.en: To combine or blend to form a single entity.

words.tr: adj. 声音甜美的；悦耳动听的
words.ex: Her mellifluous voice made everyone calm.
words.ex_cn: 她悦耳的声音让每个人都平静下来。
words.en: A mellifluous sound or voice is smooth and pleasant to listen to.

words.ex: The movie is a melodrama with crying and loud arguments.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影是一部充满哭泣和激烈争吵的煽情剧。
words.en: A melodrama is a dramatic work in which the plot, typically sensational and designed to appeal strongly to the emotions, takes precedence over detailed characterization.

words.tr: adj. 撒谎的；不真实的；捏造的
words.ex: She was known for her mendacious stories.
words.ex_cn: 她以编造虚假故事而闻名。
words.en: If someone is mendacious, they are not telling the truth.

words.tr: adj. 仆人的；枯燥的；琐碎的
words.ex: He did menial work to earn money.
words.ex_cn: 他做琐碎的工作来赚钱。
words.en: A menial task is one that is considered to be lowly or degrading, often involving physical work and requiring little skill or education.

words.tr:
adj. 唯利是图的；雇佣的
n. 雇佣兵；唯利是图者
words.ex: He works as a mercenary for money.
words.ex_cn: 他为了钱当雇佣兵。
words.en: A mercenary is a professional soldier hired to serve in a foreign army.

words.tr:
adj. 多汞的；含汞的；易变的；灵活的；反复无常的
n. 汞制剂；水银剂
words.ex: His mercurial mood changes from happy to angry quickly.
words.ex_cn: 他多汞的情绪很快从高兴变到生气。
words.en: If you describe someone as mercurial, you mean that they frequently change their mind or mood without warning.

words.tr: v. 施以催眠术；迷住；迷惑
words.ex: The dancer mesmerized the crowd with her slow movements.
words.ex_cn: 舞者用她缓慢的动作对观众施以催眠术。
words.en: If you are mesmerized by something, you are so interested in it or so attracted to it that you cannot think about anything else.

words.tr: adj. 流星的；大气的；昙花一现的；辉煌而短暂的
words.ex: The meteoric rise of the new star surprised everyone.
words.ex_cn: 这位新星的流星般崛起让所有人感到惊讶。
words.en: If you use meteoric to describe something such as a rise to fame, you mean it happens very quickly and is very noticeable.

words.tr: adj. 一丝不苟的；缜密的
words.ex: He is meticulous about checking his homework.
words.ex_cn: 他仔细检查作业。
words.en: If you describe someone as meticulous, you mean that they do things very carefully and with great attention to detail.

words.tr:
v. （使）生气
n. 发脾气；微怒
words.ex: She got a miff when I forgot her birthday.
words.ex_cn: 我忘记了她的生日，她有点恼火。
words.en: To cause to be annoyed or offended.

words.ex: He feels comfortable in his artistic milieu.
words.ex_cn: 他在他的艺术环境中感到自在。
words.en: The milieu is the environment or setting in which something happens or develops.

words.ex: He performed a mime on the street.
words.ex_cn: 他在街上表演了哑剧。
words.en: A mime is a form of performance art where the performer uses gestures and movements without speech to convey a story or emotion. As a verb, to mime means to imitate or mimic actions or expressions without using words.

words.ex: The boss treated his minion like a servant.
words.ex_cn: 老板把他的手下当仆人对待。
words.en: A minion is a servile follower or subordinate of a powerful person, especially a political leader.

words.ex: The minuscule dot was hard to see with the naked eye.
words.ex_cn: 那个极小的点用肉眼很难看到。
words.en: If you describe something as minuscule, you mean that it is very small.

words.tr:
n. 泥潭；泥沼；困境
v. 使陷进泥坑里
words.ex: The car got stuck in the mire.
words.ex_cn: 汽车陷在泥沼里了。
words.en: Mire refers to an area of wet, soggy ground or a difficult situation from which it is hard to extricate oneself.

words.ex: The children laughed with mirth.
words.ex_cn: 孩子们带着欢乐大笑。
words.en: Mirth is amusement which you express by laughing.

words.tr: n. 厌恶世人者；遁世者
words.ex: He is a misanthrope who avoids people.
words.ex_cn: 他是一个避世的人，不喜欢与人交往。
words.en: A misanthrope is someone who dislikes and avoids other people.

words.ex: He lost his keys by a mischance.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心弄丢了钥匙。
words.en: An unlucky event or accident.

words.tr: adj. 调皮的；恶作剧的；有害的
words.ex: The mischievous boy laughed and hid his sister's shoes.
words.ex_cn: 那个顽皮的男孩笑着藏起了他姐姐的鞋子。
words.en: If you describe someone or their behaviour as mischievous, you mean that they enjoy playing tricks on people or doing things to annoy or embarrass them.

words.ex: He misconstrued her smile as anger.
words.ex_cn: 他误解了她的微笑，以为是生气。
words.en: If you misconstrue something that has been said or something that happens, you interpret it wrongly.

words.ex: The miscreant was caught red-handed.
words.ex_cn: 那个恶棍被当场抓住。
words.en: A miscreant is someone who behaves badly or does not obey the law.

words.tr: n. 行为不端；轻罪；不轨行为
words.ex: He committed a minor misdemeanour last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周犯了一个轻微的罪行。
words.en: A misdemeanour is an act that is not very serious and is often punished by a fine or a short period of imprisonment.

words.tr: adj. 吝啬的；小气的；少量的
words.ex: He was miserly with his money and never spent a penny on others.
words.ex_cn: 他对钱很吝啬，从不为别人花一分钱。
words.en: If you say that someone is miserly, you disapprove of them because they seem to hate spending money, and to spend as little as possible.

words.tr:
n. 疑虑；怀疑
v. 使疑虑；使担忧；“misgive”的现在分词
words.ex: He had a misgiving about the plan.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个计划感到不安。
words.en: A misgiving is a feeling of doubt or anxiety about something that might happen or might have happened.

words.tr: n. 不幸之事；灾祸；恶运
words.ex: He had a little mishap when he dropped his coffee.
words.ex_cn: 他不小心把咖啡洒了，出了点小差错。
words.en: A mishap is an unlucky accident.

words.tr: n. 螨；小虫；极小量；小家伙
words.ex: A mite is very small and lives on animals.
words.ex_cn: 螨虫非常小，生活在动物身上。
words.en: A mite is a very small creature which is related to spiders. There are many different kinds of mites, some of which can cause diseases in plants, animals, and humans.

words.ex: Planting trees can mitigate air pollution.
words.ex_cn: 植树可以减轻空气污染。
words.en: To mitigate something means to make it less unpleasant, serious, or painful.

words.tr:
v. 呻吟；呼啸；抱怨
n. 呻吟声；萧萧声；抱怨
words.ex: He moans when he is tired.
words.ex_cn: 他累了的时候会呻吟。
words.en: If you moan, you make a low sound, usually because you are unhappy or in pain.

words.ex: He ate a moderate amount of food.
words.ex_cn: 他吃了适量的食物。
words.en: If you moderate something or if it moderates, it becomes less extreme or violent, or if you moderate a discussion, you help the people in it to reach an agreement.

words.tr: n. 少量；一点点；一小份
words.ex: He had a modicum of common sense.
words.ex_cn: 他有一点点常识。
words.en: A modicum of something, especially something that is good or desirable, is a small but useful or significant amount of it.

words.ex: He will modify the plan tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天会更改计划。
words.en: To change something slightly, especially in order to make it more suitable for a particular purpose.

words.ex: The monarch ruled the country for 50 years.
words.ex_cn: 这位君主统治这个国家长达50年。
words.en: A monarch is a king, queen, emperor, or empress.

words.tr: adj.  独块巨石的；整体的；庞大的；单一的；统一的
words.ex: The ancient temple was built from a monolithic stone.
words.ex_cn: 这座古代神庙是由一块巨石建成的。
words.en: A monolithic structure is extremely large and made of one piece or one type of material.

words.tr: n. 独白；独角戏；长篇大论
words.ex: He gave a monologue on stage.
words.ex_cn: 他在舞台上发表了一段独白。
words.en: A monologue is a long speech by one person, especially in a play or film, or a long speech by one person during a conversation.

words.ex: The big company tries to monopolize the market.
words.ex_cn: 这家大公司试图垄断市场。
words.en: If a company or person monopolizes something, they have complete control over it, so that other people cannot share it.

words.tr: n. 蒙太奇；画面剪辑；合成画；大杂烩
words.ex: The movie ends with a montage of old photos.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影以一组旧照片的蒙太奇结尾。
words.en: A montage is a technique in film editing in which a series of short shots are edited into a sequence to condense space, time, and information.

words.tr: adj. 病态的；心理不健康的
words.ex: He has a morbid fear of the dark.
words.ex_cn: 他对黑暗有一种病态的恐惧。
words.en: If you describe a person or their interest in something as morbid, you mean that they are very interested in unpleasant things, especially death, and you think this is strange.

words.tr:
adj. 尖刻的；刻薄的；尖锐讥讽的
n. 媒染剂
words.ex: His mordant wit made everyone laugh.
words.ex_cn: 他尖刻的幽默让大家笑了。
words.en: A mordant remark is one that is critical and sarcastic. In chemistry, a mordant is a substance used to set dyes on fabrics or tissue sections by forming a coordination complex with the dye which then attaches to the fabric or tissue.

words.tr: adj. 濒临死亡的；垂死的；
words.ex: The moribund patient stopped breathing.
words.ex_cn: 这位濒临死亡的病人停止了呼吸。
words.en: If you describe something as moribund, you mean that it is in a very bad condition and is not active or successful.

words.tr: adj. 郁闷的；抑郁的；孤僻的
words.ex: He was morose after losing his job.
words.ex_cn: 他失业后变得忧郁。
words.en: If you describe someone as morose, you mean that they are very unhappy, bad-tempered, and unwilling to talk or be sociable.

words.ex: He was mortified when he forgot his lines on stage.
words.ex_cn: 当他忘记舞台上的台词时，他感到非常羞愧。
words.en: To mortify someone means to cause them to feel very embarrassed or ashamed. To mortify a part of your body means to discipline it by denying it things that it wants or needs.

words.ex: The motif of love appears in many poems.
words.ex_cn: 爱的主题出现在许多诗歌中。
